summary: A fresh install has no project: the first migration creates default_project only when an older database already holds data; get_default_project_id() never creates a project; calls that need a project raise NoProject (HTTP 400, reason_code no_project); /api/home and /api/state answer 200 {no_project:true}; the desktop backend no longer seeds the 10 world-model papers or fetches on first start; a project without keywords asks no source; the legacy world-model recipe, legacy pins and seed fallback belong only to the literal id default_project.
scope_note: Worktree onboarding-tour, step A of the onboarding plan, on top of update-check b7cb191. Backend only: the front end is wired in a later step (page redirect to project creation when there is no project), so until then a fresh install shows the old main page without data. Migration rule changed without a new migration number; existing databases are untouched (default_project already exists).

budget_impact.rationale: Removes a first-start network fetch (manual_refresh of the world-model recipe) and removes the bundled seed list from the packaged app; adds no model call, prompt, retry or token.
budget_impact.before: first start seeded 10 papers and fetched OpenAlex/arXiv in the background
budget_impact.after: first start does nothing until the person creates a project

open_risks: Behaviour changes for existing users, written in HANDOFF: deleting every project now leaves none (the page must send the person to project creation); a project with no keywords no longer falls back to the world-model search (only the migrated default_project does); legacy global pins are no longer given to the newest project.
The front end does not handle no_project yet (later step); a fresh install is unusable in the UI until then.
A real first launch of the packaged app on an empty data directory was not run (no build, by instruction); the subprocess test covers the source backend only.
